transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Janelle (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM); Eli (Mosaic Head of ML), Maria (CPO), Tom (Infra), Avery (Data Eng)

[00:00] Janelle: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Janelle with Redwood, Samir our solutions engineer is on, Lena our CSM. Eli, Maria, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Eli: yeah thanks, we wanna focus on the cost side today, like per token unit economics, and what levers we can pull to keep within a 20-25k monthly budget.
[00:28] Samir: great, we can walk hosted vs dedicated vs private and show how batching, KV cache/prefix cache, and quantization change the numbers. rough ok if i ask about your current volumes and prompt lengths?
[00:40] Tom: sure, currently about 2k QPS at peak for inference gateway, but most requests are low QPS spikes. avg prompt 120 tokens, avg completion 40 tokens, so roughly 160 tokens per call.
[00:55] Maria: and we have a hard constraint on tail latency, 200ms 95th for the UI flows, background jobs can be slower.
[01:05] Samir: noted. For starters, hosted per token pricing we typically quote varies by model class - small open models vs large dense models. For a mid tier model you'd see e.g. $0.0009 per 1k tokens for hosted generation - sorry those are example numbers - and dedicated reserved capacity can drop effective unit cost 20-40% depending on commit.
[01:32] Eli: can you break down the math? like how batching really helps?
[01:36] Samir: yeah. so batching pools inference requests to amortize the kernel launch and attention overhead. if you can accept a few extra ms of latency you can get 1.8x-3x throughput improvement depending on sequence lengths. example: at our 160 token average, batching 4-8 requests together reduces per token GPU cost because the transformer compute overlaps. also continuous KV caching for multi turn prompts can slash repeated prefix tokens - in some finance workflows we see 30-70% token reduction because the prompt prefix stays the same.
[02:05] Eli: hmm 30-70% is big. but our UI path is single-shot queries, caching won't help there.
[02:12] Samir: understood. then batching and quantization become more important. 4-bit quantization (we call low bit profiles) often gives 1.7x-2x inference speed up and memory savings compared to fp16, which translates to cost reduction since you fit more instances per GPU. quality tradeoffs vary by model and you should run evals.
[02:32] Maria: what's the delta if we go dedicated? like committed GPUs vs hosted?
[02:36] Janelle: dedicated (reserved) provides predictable throughput and discounts. for example, a monthly commit can shift per token effective cost down by ~25% if your utilization is high - but if you underutilize you pay for the capacity. Redwood Dedicated also gives you configurable autoscaling and burst capacity so you can cover traffic spikes, and per route SLAs.
[02:54] Tom: ok, we are very sensitive to peak cost since infra budgets are fixed. any ability to burst on hosted and only reserve minimal dedicated?
[03:02] Samir: yes, hybrid routing is a common pattern. route SLO critical traffic to dedicated and less critical or overflow to hosted. the runtime supports policy based routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
[03:13] Avery: quick Q on data residency - if we do private, can we host on our cloud account in eu-west?
[03:20] Janelle: yes, Redwood Private supports customer VPC and on prem options. we support key management integrations (KMS/HSM) and audit logs.
[03:29] Eli: back to math, say we target 25k per month. what's feasible with your numbers?
[03:34] Samir: okay rough sketch. start with usage: assume 1M requests / month at 160 tokens = 160M tokens. at hosted base example rate of $0.0009 per 1k tokens that's $144 effective - wait let me recalc - 160M tokens / 1k = 160k units * $0.0009 = $144... that sounds off; oh right because $0.0009 per 1k tokens is very cheap example, let me give clearer realistic tiers: hosted for a large open model often ranges $0.005 - $0.02 per 1k tokens depending on model. if we pick $0.008 per 1k as a mid example, 160M tokens would be $1,280. that is still well under 25k - so either your volumes are bigger or i'm missing something.
[04:16] Maria: yeah our projected volume for feature rollout is much larger - we expect 20M requests / month at peak in future. realtime product will be 2-3M calls/day.
[04:27] Samir: that changes things. 20M requests * 160 tokens = 3.2B tokens/month. at $0.008 per 1k tokens => 3.2M * $0.008 = $25,600. so that approximates your 25k target. But then batching and quantization can reduce that. if you enable 2x effective savings from batching+quant, you get to ~12.8k/month.
[04:56] Eli: ok that math is helpful. what's realistic to achieve 2x savings?
[04:59] Samir: depends on latency SLO. if UI needs <200ms p95, batching headroom is limited. but quantization (4 bit) and model selection (smaller causal models tuned for generation) can cut cost ~1.5-2x, and caching for background and multi turn flows can add more. we usually run a short benchmark to measure real world speedups for your exact prompt mix.
[05:20] Tom: what about minimum commitment sizes for dedicated? like how many GPUs and cost?
[05:25] Janelle: typical starting commit for Dedicated is 2-4 GPU equivalents for smaller pilots. price varies by region and GPU class; commit discounts scale with size and term. we can show a 12 month reserved example vs on demand hosted numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:38] Maria: regulatory Q - do you keep logs? we need auditability and ability to purge data.
[05:45] Lena: we have configurable retention, audit logs, and support customer managed keys in Private deployments. we'll share SOC2 and network diagram.
[05:53] Eli: competitors - have you benchmarked against OpenAI's hosted endpoints for cost?
[05:57] Samir: yes we publish comparative perf/cost for common workloads. results vary by model and sequence length. our selling point is you get the same API across hosted/dedicated/private plus better control over batching, KV caching and routing policies that can materially cut unit costs.
[06:12] Avery: one technical detail - how do you handle KV cache syncing for private clusters? we have multi AZ.
[06:18] Samir: KV cache is local to the serving shard; for multi AZ you can configure sticky routing or use shared cache layers. For private we provide options; some customers accept slight cold starts between AZs. we'll cover arch in deep dive.
[06:32] Tom: what telemetry will you need from our side for the benchmark?
[06:35] Samir: traces of request size distribution, target p95 latency, percent of multi turn sessions, concurrency patterns. you can drop anonymized logs or a small sample.
[06:45] Eli: timeline - we want to validate before Q2 feature launch, so need pilot in next 2 weeks.
[06:50] Janelle: doable. propose a 2 week pilot: week 1 run benchmarks with your test harness; week 2 run a short production canary on hosted/dedicated routing. Samir: I'll provision the test ingest and provide a harness.
[07:05] Maria: any gotchas on cost modeling? we hate surprises.
[07:09] Samir: main surprises are tail flags: underutilized reserved capacity, model changes that increase tokens per request (longer completions), and retries / warmup overheads. we include cold start and burst estimates in the spreadsheet. Also note that per request orchestration like tool calling or external API calls can add wall time but not token cost.
[07:29] Eli: curious about quantization quality regressions for our finance prompts - risk tolerance is low.
[07:34] Samir: we recommend an eval set of your prompts. many customers A/B quantized vs fp16 for scoring on precision metrics. often you get acceptable quality at 4 bit for many open models, but for high precision scoring you might keep fp16. it's workload dependent.
[07:49] Maria: ok, can you include in the deck a sample model matrix: small/medium/large with expected per token cost and latency ranges?
[07:55] Janelle: yes, we'll include that + dedicated commit scenarios.
[08:00] Tom: one more infra ask: will the benchmark simulate our concurrency patterns? we need realistic tail behaviour.
[08:06] Samir: yes we'll take your p90/p95 concurrency traces and replay at scale.
[08:12] Janelle: quick recap: we will send cost model and pricing sheet, Samir will run benchmarks, Lena shares SOC2 and VPC docs, and Mosaic sends token distribution traces. next sync to review pilot results and decide on dedicated commit.
[08:28] Eli: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:32] Janelle: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis hears (e.g., V P C spelled out in notes). References: pricing deck (link:n/a), benchmark harness (link:n/a).
